title: Sharp project settings
description: The settings of a Sharp project (sharpc -P <folder>). The compiler reads them in lib/compiler/configuration/settings_processor.sharp; keep this file in step with it.

compiler.description: The C++ compiler: the path of g++ or clang++, or the name of one on the PATH. Without it: the SHARP_CXX environment variable, then a search (the PATH, then where MinGW is usually installed).

flags.description: Extra flags for the C++ compiler. They come after the ones Sharp gives itself (-shared, -std=c++17, -static on Windows, -fPIC elsewhere), so yours win: "-std=c++20", "-O2".

include.description: Folders that hold only header files (-I), as paths inside the project or absolute: another library's headers. The "sources" folders are searched for headers already - they are not named again here.

libraries.description: More libraries to link (-l), by name: "ws2_32", "m".

sources.description: C++ files or folders for this system only: compiled, and searched for header files.
C++ files or folders for this processor only: compiled, and searched for header files. Two folders with the same file names - one per processor - do not meet.

processors.description: Settings for one kind of processor, added only when the C++ compiler builds for it. The system and the processor are separate: ARM runs Linux and Windows. Written at the top of the toolchain it counts on every system; inside "windows" / "linux", for that processor on that system.

arm.description: Every ARM processor, 32 and 64 bit (a Raspberry Pi): the libraries of its hardware go here.

x86.description: Every Intel / AMD processor, 32 and 64 bit (a PC).

name.description: The project's name (shown by the IDE and in messages).

version.description: The version written into the executable (-v).

output.description: The name of the executable: it is written to build/outputs/<output> (-o).

compile_only.description: true: check the program and write no executable (-c).

show_all_errors.description: true: show every error, not only the first of each kind (-a).

debug.description: true: keep the source text in the executable for stack traces (-dbg); false: leave it out (-R).

release.description: true: a release build - no source text in the executable and the names obfuscated (-R -obf).

obfuscate.description: true: rename everything the `obfuscate` blocks do not keep (-obf).

cache_files.description: false: do not keep or read the build cache (-cacheoff).

target.description: The platform version the program is built for (-target).

target_api.description: The version of the installed standard library to build with, for example "0.4.3".

enable_warnings.description: Kinds of warning to turn on, by name.

disable_warnings.description: Kinds of warning to turn off, by name.

warnings_as_errors.description: true: every warning stops the build (-werror).

error_limit.description: How many errors are shown before the compiler stops (-errlmt).

green_mode.description: true: use less memory and fewer threads while compiling (-g).

magic_mode.description: A switch of the compiler for its own development.

compiler_debug_mode.description: true: the compiler prints what it is doing (for working on the compiler itself).

ignore_files.description: Files that are not part of the program: paths inside the project, or as written (-ignore).

ignore_folders.description: Folders that are not part of the program, for example "build" (-ignoredir).

extern_lib.description: Folders of Sharp libraries the program is compiled with (-L). A project that names none gets the installed standard library.

ignore_extern_files.description: Files of the libraries that are left out, with paths as written.

ignore_extern_folders.description: Folders of the libraries that are left out, with paths as written.

c_libraries.description: Which file each C library of the program's `extern "name" { }` blocks is: a file's name the system finds, or a path - absolute, or from the project's folder. One text or a list for every system, or an object with a text or a list per system.

native.description: The C++ of the project's `native` functions (the Sharp Native Interface). With "sources" the compiler builds it into build/outputs/<group>.dll (.so on Linux) on every build.

sources.description: The C++ files, or folders of them (their whole tree), as paths inside the project: [ "src/cpp" ]. Each folder is also searched for header files.

toolchain.description: The C++ compiler and its flags. Everything in it is optional: without a toolchain the compiler finds g++ or clang++ itself.

windows.description: The same four settings, used on Windows only: "compiler" replaces the one above, the lists are added to it.

linux.description: The same four settings, used on Linux only: "compiler" replaces the one above, the lists are added to it.
